**Root cause (measured, not guessed - the tier race):** the hermetic server IS the real one (server/serve.py `_fit_worker` -> tools/site_done.py's one-site line): the line builds the overlay FIRST (depictions.json gains the entry) and re-scores the site SECOND (build_site.set_drawings rewrites sites.json - the score is computed FROM the built overlays by marks()/overlays(), so this order is mandatory). Retained B tree (pytest-0/awowner0) timeline: doc write 01:57:15.802, base overlay :16.816, ink overlay :23.309, **depictions.json :23.310, sites.json :23.429 (119 ms), review.json :23.846**. web/index.html `saveFit()` polls depictions.json every 1.5 s and, when the saved depiction appears, fetches sites.json ONCE, adopts drawings/score/oldest/overlays and sets the marker class from that one fetch, then stops. A poll landing in the 119 ms gap adopts the pre-rescore score and the marker keeps its old tier until a manual reload (the owner would see the wrong square tier). B's poll landed in the gap (t1 adopted); A's landed after the re-score (t2 adopted) - hence the per-save flake. Not fixable on the test side (the page's one-shot adoption is done; a longer probe poll cannot un-adopt it), not fixable by reordering the pipeline (the re-score reads the built depictions), so the fix is the page's adoption (245).
